scope: Eleven numbered additions: four finite-group convex/robust statements, three simultaneous-positivity/mean-contrast statements and four return-geometry/physical-dictionary approximation statements. This is not eleven independent discovery claims.

source_verification.scope: Author catalog, identity and dependency consistency; not a proof checker, native build, priority clearance or independent assessment.

statements.claim_class: A convex-specification extension of the retained exact stochastic normal form, with arbitrary original stochastic controllers and explicit pure/mixed resource accounting. Classical stochastic-semigroup and simplex structure is credited rather than claimed as new.
classical_ingredients: Finite Markov-chain recurrent classes and lazy convergence
Affine automorphisms of a finite simplex permute its vertices
Closed convex sets are preserved under finite averaging and limits
statements.conclusion: The complete all-word convex specification is realizable with at most M labels exactly when a finite G-set X, a probability preparation lambda and stochastic decoder D meet all finite constraints lambda P_g D in K_g with cost |X|+1_{lambda nonpoint}<=M for pure starts, or |X|<=M for mixed starts. The approximating action may be nonfaithful.
hypotheses: A finite command alphabet A, finite group G, a supplied surjective homomorphism gamma:A*->G, and finite output set C.
For every g, a closed convex subset K_g of the fixed probability simplex Delta(C); empty constraints are permitted.

The original arbitrary stochastic controller satisfies e_o Q_w D_0 in K_gamma(w) for every word, including the empty word. It is not assumed to satisfy group relations on its hidden or observable states.
Pure starts count their prescribed initial label; mixed starts allow a free initial probability row.
statements.identity: R76 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
statements.label: thm:r76-convex-normal-form
statements.limits: All words representing each group element are constrained; checking only one representative per group element on the original machine is insufficient. Convexity and closedness are used in the limiting argument. This is not a classification of arbitrary nonrigid optimal stopping or feedback.
statements.proof: A finite identity-word edge cover yields a lazy stochastic average and recurrent projection E. Every identity word preserves its closed classes and satisfies E Q_l E=E. Inverse-word sandwiches give simplex automorphisms, representative independence and the group law. Two-sided identity-word averaging keeps the output inside each closed convex K_g, without assuming exact output factorization in the original machine. Closed-class counting preserves the initializer cost; a direct initializer gives the converse.

statements.claim_class: An exact reduction of a synthesis optimum over all stochastic machines and all words to finite compact optimization, including the initializer alternative. The algebraic elimination machinery is classical.
classical_ingredients: Compactness of finite products of probability simplexes
Real algebraic quantifier elimination and sample-point construction
statements.conclusion: The unrestricted stochastic uniform-error optimum equals a finite minimum over G-actions of bounded degree. Mixed starts minimize d_X over |X|<=M; pure starts minimize point preparations on |X|<=M and arbitrary preparations on |X|<=M-1. The minima are attained and 1-Lipschitz in the target table. Algebraic targets admit computable optimal values and realizing tables by real quantifier elimination.
hypotheses: A supplied target b:G->Delta(C) on a finite group and an integer label budget M>=1.
Error is the supremum of total variation over every command word representing G; the pure and mixed start conventions are separate.
For computability only, the target table is given exactly by real algebraic entries.
statements.identity: R76 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
statements.label: thm:r76-minimax-normal-form
statements.limits: This is a supplied finite-group target synthesis theorem. It does not decide cutpoint, isolation or equivalence problems for an arbitrary supplied probabilistic automaton. No polynomial-time complexity, executed general quantifier elimination, or matching bit/precision/workspace bound is claimed.
statements.proof: Use closed total-variation balls as the convex specifications, then enumerate the finitely many finite G-actions up to the given degree. Compact preparations and decoders give attainment; the triangle inequality gives Lipschitz continuity and robustness. Polynomial inequalities with auxiliary absolute-value variables encode each finite optimization, and elimination plus algebraic sample points give the stated effective synthesis.

statements.title: Attained finite optimization for infinite-word error

statements.claim_class: Explicit robustness and initialization certificates for arbitrary all-word approximating stochastic machines after the new convex normal form. The matrix rank inequality and representation-theoretic ingredients are classical and proved or credited directly.
classical_ingredients: Fourier averaging over a finite group
statements.conclusion: A realizing action of multiplicity m_rho has sigma_{m_rho+1}(A_rho(b))<=sqrt(2) delta; for a binary scalar block the bound is delta. Thresholded singular-value ranks give an integer permutation-module covering lower bound for every approximating stochastic controller. Below half the residual separation, a pure controller with fewer than N labels requires one additional initializer beyond that lower bound.
hypotheses: The finite-group target and all-word total-variation error convention of the preceding theorems, with the retained normalized stacked Fourier blocks A_rho(b).
For the strengthened pure-start bound, N>1 distinct residual tables, their minimum nonzero max-total-variation separation Delta_b, error delta<Delta_b/2, and total label count less than N.
The integer cover contains at least one orbit; multiplicities include any irreducible representation type.
statements.identity: R76 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
statements.label: thm:r76-robust-multiplicity
statements.limits: These are rigorous lower bounds, not claimed sharp uniform-error constants for every target. The half-separation and fewer-than-N hypotheses are essential to the additional pure-start charge; it is not an unconditional +1 theorem for every approximation.
statements.proof: The positive and negative parts of each probability-row error have mass at most delta, giving stacked Euclidean norm at most sqrt(2)delta. Averaging against unitary representations bounds Fourier operator error. A nullspace/right-singular-vector intersection proves the rank approximation inequality directly. Orbit multiplicity counting gives the cover; a point preparation would merge two separated target residuals if its orbit were too small, proving the initialization charge.

statements.claim_class: An exact error frontier illustrating the arbitrary-controller minimax reduction; the elementary orbit classification is not a new group theorem.
classical_ingredients: Orbit-stabilizer theorem for a prime cyclic group
Chebyshev center of a real interval
statements.conclusion: For either initialization convention the error is the Chebyshev radius of the set of target rows when M<p, and zero when M>=p. For binary outputs that radius is half the range of the first-coordinate response.
hypotheses: G=C_p for a prime p, any probability target b, and integer memory budget M>=1, with uniform error over all words.
statements.identity: R76 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
statements.label: cor:r76-prime-error
statements.limits: The statement is for prime cyclic groups and the fixed all-word error. It is not an expected-cost approximation or the original general-M squared-sign decision-risk curve.
statements.proof: A prime cyclic group has only point or p-point orbits. Below p labels every action is trivial and gives a constant response; a one-label Chebyshev center attains its best error. A point-prepared regular p-orbit realizes any target exactly.

statements.title: Uniform error cannot replace a prime orbit

statements.claim_class: A sharp joint positivity inequality and full equality classification extending the retained one-outcome singular extremum. It is proved explicitly and is not asserted to be an exhaustively priority-cleared classical matrix theorem.
statements.conclusion: The weighted sum gamma C+D is at least [gamma(n+1)+n^2-2n-1+2 sqrt(n(gamma-1)(gamma+n-2))]/(n-1). Equality is exactly the stated simultaneous permutation of v=(M,...,M,-m) and its unique c,d, with m=sqrt((gamma+n-2)/(n(gamma-1))) and M=(1+m)/(n-1).
hypotheses: n>=5, real vectors v,c,d with sum(v)=1, v.c=v.d=0, and c_i>=v_j-delta_ij, d_i>=delta_ij-v_j for every i,j.
gamma>=2(n-2)/(n-4); no sign assumption on v or symmetry of any associated coefficient matrix.
statements.identity: R76 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
statements.label: lem:r76-simultaneous-positivity
statements.limits: The shared null vector and the gamma range are part of the theorem. Two unrelated nonnegative singular matrices do not automatically satisfy this common-preparation constraint.
statements.proof: A common null vector gives simultaneous lower bounds for both outcome sums. Bounding squared coordinates between their extreme values and combining with the retained first-outcome estimate reduces the weighted sum to a strictly concave quadratic in its largest coordinate. The left endpoint is minimized by AM-GM; an explicit positive polynomial separates the other endpoint for all n>=5 and gamma in the stated range. Equality in each step fixes the unique negative coordinate and all excess supports.

statements.title: Sharp simultaneous positivity inequality

statements.claim_class: An exact parameter-feasibility region for a bounded centered matrix problem, with matching positive synthesis and the stated boundary rigidity. Standard nonnegative-factor support reasoning is credited as an ingredient.
classical_ingredients: Common left nullspace and double centering
Ordinary rank lower bounds for positive factorizations
statements.conclusion: Existence of a joined-rank-deficient bounded centered pair, existence of such a pair with a common positive factorization of width n-1, and a<=F_n(p) are equivalent. F_n has the three explicitly matched branches with junctions p0=1/(n-sqrt(n)) and p1=2/n. All width-(n-1) boundary factorizations are classified on the low and middle intervals; the middle-interval coefficient pair is unique up to simultaneous coordinate permutation.
hypotheses: n>=5, 0<p<1, a>0 and P=I-J/n.
Existential coefficient pairs (A,u) with u a probability column, 0<=A<=u 1^T, total entry sum np, PAP=aP, and joined ordinary rank rank[A u]<n.
The proposed positive factors use n-1 probability preparations, a probability orbit-weight row and first-output decoder rows in [0,1]^n.
statements.identity: R76 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
statements.label: thm:r76-bounded-coefficients
statements.limits: The equivalence is existential: it does not say every feasible off-boundary matrix pair admits width n-1. Joined rank is stronger than separate singularity of the two outcomes. Full factorization classification is asserted only on the specified low/middle boundary, not on every feasible matrix or every stochastic implementation.
statements.proof: Joined rank gives one normalized common left null vector for A and its complementary outcome B=u1^T-A, producing the simultaneous vector inequalities and C=p/a,D=(1-p)/a. The retained singular bound controls low means; a tuned weighted joint bound controls middle means; direct feasibility controls large means. Explicit common positive factors attain each boundary and decoder mixing fills the smaller contrasts. Equality and nonnegative zero-pattern/ratio arguments classify the boundary factors and force equal weights in the middle interval.

statements.title: Sharp synthesis for bounded centered coefficients

statements.claim_class: A complete two-parameter exact resource law derived from the new joint-positivity matrix theorem and retained arbitrary-core reduction. It extends the old fixed-mean model without relabelling its special case as new.
classical_ingredients: Character orthogonality and the standard S_n representation
statements.conclusion: At a=0 both minima are one. Otherwise with q=p for a>0 and q=1-p for a<0, the exact core is n(n-1) for |a|<=F_n(q), and n^2 above; the pure count adds one. Every nonconstant table keeps observable group S_n, residual count n!, and dimension 1+(n-1)^2. The nontrivial low/middle transition has precisely the classified minimum permutation-core factors; for positive contrast and p>=2/n all feasible contrasts use the smaller core.
hypotheses: n>=5 and binary S_n table beta_{p,a}=p+a(chi_n-1) satisfying 0<=p-a<=1 and 0<=p+(n-1)a<=1.
All finite stochastic exact controllers are allowed. The positive-core reduction permits every finite action, and pure initialization is counted.
The mean p is an average terminal probability over G, not a prior on an unknown model.
statements.identity: R76 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
statements.label: thm:r76-mean-contrast
statements.limits: Boundary factor rigidity concerns minimum permutation cores. This is not a full high-contrast classification for every finite group, an unknown-model recovery theorem, an arbitrary-prior decision-risk solution, or a claim of minimal quantum dimension.
statements.proof: The faithful full standard block preserves the observable invariants and the retained subgroup-index lower bounds at every nonzero contrast. Any core below n^2 reduces to n-1 natural orbits after absorbing noncarrying constant contributions. Its common preparation gives the bounded joined-rank coefficient problem, so the matrix theorem gives the exact threshold. Explicit n-orbit decoders give the upper throughout feasibility; output complementation handles negative contrast, and the retained pure-start formula supplies the counted initializer.

statements.claim_class: A sharp adaptive expected-budget event bound built from a classical waiting-time potential. It is not claimed as invention of the Bernoulli run waiting-time formula.
classical_ingredients: Initial randomization under an expected-cost constraint
statements.conclusion: P(eta_L<=tau)<=min{1,(1-r)B/(r^{-L}-1)}. The coefficient is sharp: independent Bernoulli continuation of probability r and an initial randomized choice whether to run until eta_L attain the stated supremum.
hypotheses: Sequential reports split into continuing and returning, with conditional continuation probability at most a fixed 0<r<1 after the entire past, current command and private randomization.
The policy may stop before calling; its call count tau has target expectation at most finite B. Eta_L is the first completion of L consecutive continuing reports, L>=1.
statements.identity: R76 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
statements.label: lem:r76-excursion-budget
statements.limits: Sharpness concerns the exceptional-run probability, not a lower bound on every simulator's approximation error. The target expected budget is not a tail or cost assertion about a second process.
statements.proof: The run-length potential u(k)=(r^{-k}-1)/(1-r) has conditional drift at most one before completion. Sum at the bounded stopping time min(tau,eta_L,H), then take the monotone event limit. For Bernoulli continuation, the drift is exactly one and bounded/monotone convergence gives E eta_L=u(L). Initial randomization provides every expected budget below that mean.

statements.title: Sharp expected-cost excursion bound

statements.claim_class: A constructive uniform stopped-law approximation theorem combining a finite return polytope, continuation-semigroup growth and an expected-cost exceptional-run bound. The positive-realization and coupling ingredients are credited separately.
classical_ingredients: Convex decomposition of normalized instrument outputs
Trace norm contraction for terminal measurements
Counting free words and commuting multi-indices
statements.conclusion: One policy-independent G(L)-label mixed model, where G(L) counts distinct normalized seed images under fewer than L continuation branches, approximates every complete stopped law and stopped classical-quantum record within min{1,(1-r)B/(r^{-L}-1)}. A counted pure start uses at most G(L)+1. General growth is bounded by k sum_{j<L} b^j; pairwise commuting continuation maps give k binomial(L+b-1,b), and any independently proved polynomial orbit growth yields a polylogarithmic label upper.
hypotheses: Finite-dimensional quantum instruments for a fixed finite nonempty command alphabet, with finite report sets; a fixed invariant closed convex state set C contains all prescribed seeds.

A finite seed polytope P contains the initial state. For every state in C and every command, total continuing-report mass is at most r<1, and every positive-mass returning normalized branch lies in P. The theorem uses 0<r<1.

Policies share only the visible record and their classical randomness, may choose commands/stopping/terminal POVMs, and have target expected call count at most B. No additional entangled quantum register is present.
statements.identity: R76 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
statements.label: thm:r76-return-approximation
statements.limits: The return geometry is an explicit hypothesis, not a consequence of average-channel mixing. The countable refinement is only a proof device. The theorem gives an upper, does not assert necessary +1 initialization or stationarity of the approximation, and does not preserve its expected duration. External policy storage and computation costs are separate.
statements.proof: A countable exact seed/continuation refinement supplies a proof coupling. The finite dictionary realizes every returning branch through seed mixtures and every represented continuing image exactly; only an overflowing continuation is redirected. First coupling failure requires L consecutive continuing reports, so the sharp event bound controls the full positive terminal-block mass. Truncation and a scalar nontermination limit yield the complete stopped classical-quantum estimate. An initializer executes the first actual command; counting words or commuting multi-indices gives the resource bounds.

statements.title: Finite-memory approximation from return geometry

statements.claim_class: An explicit complete-instrument consequence of the new general return-geometry theorem. It separates exact noisy-memory scaling from approximation of target-budget-bounded stopped laws, without declaring the earlier exact noise law a new result.
classical_ingredients: Exact field operations with algebraic rotation entries
statements.conclusion: One common model uses at most 3 binomial(L+a-1,a) mixed or one more pure labels and has complete stopped-law/classical-quantum error at most min{1,7B/[8(8^L-1)]}. Choosing L=max{1,ceil(log_8(1+7B/(8delta)))} gives error delta. A single angle needs at most 3L+1 pure labels, uniformly in its value; fixed finite alphabets have a polylogarithmic upper. The explicit table is algebraic under algebraic rotation data.
hypotheses: The retained complete three-report qubit instrument at alpha=1, initial state I/2, and a fixed known finite angle alphabet of size a>=1.
The same visible adaptive stopping/command/terminal-POVM policies and target expected budget as in the return-geometry theorem; no extra entangled register.
For the exact coefficient claim only, every supplied angle has algebraic sine and cosine.
statements.identity: R76 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
statements.label: cor:r76-qubit-polylog
statements.limits: The angle alphabet is fixed and finite; this dictionary does not uniformly cover a continuum of command angles. No unrestricted classical lower approximation rate or expected-duration bound for the approximation is proved; the subsequent matching physical-dictionary theorem imposes a fixed Born-decoder representation and a badly approximable single phase. Algebraic tables do not give free exact sampling, program bits or working storage. At B=0 the separate one-label zero-call realization applies.
statements.proof: Three equilateral-triangle seeds contain the radius-1/2 Bloch disk; the reset branch is one seed and the complementary branch stays within radius 5/11. The real Bloch plane is an invariant convex state set. Commuting angle rotations identify continuation words by their multi-index. Explicit return masses reconstruct the correct Bloch vector and have margin at least 1/48; only the Lth successive zero overflow is altered. Apply r=1/8 to the general theorem and account for the initializer.

statements.title: Uniform finite-alphabet approximation

statements.claim_class: A matching leading approximation law within an explicitly restricted physical-state representation class, with a separately proved counted-initialization lower and explicit quadratic-irrational instance. The classical metric and Diophantine ingredients are not claimed as new, and the result does not certify priority over all prior approximation literature.
classical_ingredients: Trace-distance duality and qubit Bloch-ball geometry
Elementary Diophantine approximation and the quadratic algebraic norm
Convex hulls of finitely many orbit points and barycentric coordinates
The preceding expected-cost excursion and return-geometry upper
statements.conclusion: Let zeta=min{1,7B/8}. For J>=2 and 0<delta<=zeta/[8^J(1+J^2/c^2)], at least J mixed-start physical labels and J+1 counted-pure-start labels are necessary. Some finite K_omega, independent of B and delta, gives matching uppers K_omega+L-1 mixed and K_omega+L pure, with L=max{1,ceil(log_8(1+7B/(8delta)))}. Thus N_phys(delta;B)/log_8(1/delta) tends to 1 for either start convention. The golden phase admits c=1/3 and K=5. The separate original algebraic rotation admits K=7 and rational tables for the upper; no badly approximable certificate for that phase is asserted.
hypotheses: The retained complete undamped three-report qubit instrument, initial state I/2, and one fixed commanded angle theta=2 pi omega, where irrational omega has a supplied constant c>0 satisfying ||q omega||_(R/Z)>=c/q for every positive integer q.

A fixed finite physical dictionary of qubit density matrices sigma_i with terminal decoder tr(E sigma_i) for every requested effect E. Report-transition tables may be arbitrary stochastic tables; they need not implement each quantum branch on every dictionary state.

One simulator approximates every common visible stopping and terminal-POVM policy within total variation delta at target expected-call budget B>0, with no extra entangled quantum register. The sharp asymptotic holds with B and omega fixed as delta decreases to zero.
statements.identity: R76 numbered author addition; the inventory includes lemmas and corollaries and is not a novelty or editorial verdict.
statements.label: thm:r76-physical-logarithm
statements.limits: The packing proof needs fixed physical density states and their Born terminal decoders. It supplies no lower for arbitrary classical hidden-state decoder tables, no uniform two-parameter asymptotic as B varies, and no asserted badly approximable certificate for the earlier algebraic rotation. The golden rotation does not satisfy the separate algebraic sine/cosine premise merely because omega is quadratic irrational. The K=7 rational construction is an upper for the original algebraic phase only. Exact-model impossibility and approximate-memory growth remain different statements.
statements.proof: A randomized prefix-testing policy for 1 followed by n zero reports has target expected cost bounded by zeta 8/7, uniformly in n. Joint prefix-mass and zero-probability terminal-failure events force one fixed physical dictionary state to have fidelity at least 1-delta/(p_n-delta) with the prepared orbit pure state. Badly approximable phase separation yields disjoint Bloch-vector balls, requiring J states; zero-call tests exclude the counted pure initializer. A finite orbit-prefix polygon contains the return disk; extending this one orbit through depth L-1 uses K+L-1 states and cannot overflow before L continuations. The return-geometry estimate gives the upper. Logarithmic comparison gives the common leading constant. An elementary quadratic norm argument and exact five-point gaps prove the golden constants; exact rational orbit coordinates and barycentric rows prove the original-phase rational upper.
